subject: general
question:
Refer to the two statements given below and select the correct option.

Statement A: Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium acetate and water.
Statement B: This reaction is neutralisation.

options.text: Both statements A and B are correct.
Statement A is correct but statement B is incorrect.
Both statements A and B are incorrect.
Statement A is incorrect but statement B is correct.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements A and B are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement A** describes the chemical reaction between **Ethanoic acid** and **sodium hydroxide**. **Ethanoic acid** (also known as **acetic acid**) has the chemical formula **CH3COOH**, and when it reacts with the strong base **sodium hydroxide** (**NaOH**), it undergoes a double displacement reaction to form **sodium acetate** (**CH3COONa**) and **water** (**H2O**). ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: **CH3COOH + NaOH → CH3COONa + H2O**.
 
• **Statement B** identifies the type of reaction. A **neutralisation** reaction is a specific type of chemical reaction where an **acid** and a **base** react with each other to produce a **salt** and **water**. Since **ethanoic acid** is an **acid** and **sodium hydroxide** is a **base**, their interaction fits this definition perfectly. ***Hence, statement B is correct.***
 
• In this **neutralisation** process, the **hydrogen ion** (H+) from the acid combines with the **hydroxide ion** (OH-) from the base to form **water**, while the remaining ions form the **ionic salt**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both statements A and B are correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ethanoic Acid (Acetic Acid):**
 
 
• It is a **weak organic acid** that is a primary component of **vinegar** (typically **5% to 8%** by volume).
 
• In its pure form, it is called **glacial acetic acid** because it freezes into ice-like crystals at a **temperature** of **16.6 degrees Celsius**.
 
• It is widely used in the **food industry** as a preservative and in the **textile industry** for the production of **synthetic fibers** like **rayon**.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (Caustic Soda):**
 
 
• It is a **strong inorganic base** and is highly **alkaline**.
 
• It is **deliquescent**, meaning it absorbs moisture and **carbon dioxide** from the air.
 
• Major **applications** include the manufacture of **soaps**, **detergents**, **paper**, and as a chemical **reagent** in laboratories.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Acetate:**
 
 
• It is the **sodium salt** of **acetic acid** and is often used as a **buffering agent** to maintain a constant **pH** in chemical reactions.
 
• It is used in **heating pads** and **hand warmers** because of its ability to release heat upon **crystallization** from a supersaturated solution.
 
• In the **food industry**, it is used as a **seasoning** (sodium diacetate) to give a salt-and-vinegar flavor to snacks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **pH Levels in Neutralisation:** Although the reaction is a **neutralisation**, the resulting **pH** of the solution depends on the strength of the reactants. When a **weak acid** (like ethanoic acid) reacts with a **strong base** (like sodium hydroxide), the resulting salt solution is slightly **alkaline**, with a **pH** greater than **7**.
 
• **Indicators:** To observe this **neutralisation** in a laboratory, indicators like **phenolphthalein** are used. The solution turns from **pink** (in base) to **colorless** as the acid is added to reach the **equivalence point**.
 
• **Exothermic Nature:** Most **neutralisation** reactions are **exothermic**, meaning they release **heat energy** to the surroundings during the process.
